v.why: A direct identity route into the output already supplies much of the benefit, so the conv on 1->3 adds less.
A parallel conv route into node 3 already supplies capacity and receptive field, so a second conv saturates.
Two conv branches summed into the output node compete for the same capacity role.
Node 2 already receives an identity copy of the input, so a conv from node 1 is a partially redundant route.
A parameter-free pooling branch leaves the output without learned features, so the direct conv adds more.
A direct conv to the output already provides capacity, so extra conv depth on the multi-hop branch has diminishing returns.
A deep conv path into node 3 already supplies learned features, so a direct conv saturates.
A strong conv route already reaches the output via node 2, so the identity shortcut adds less.
With edge 4 removed, node 1 reaches the output only through edge 2, so the conv there carries more weight.
Node 2 already carries conv-processed features from the input, so a further conv on 2->3 saturates.
